subject: biology
title: Practical: extracting DNA from fruit
key_idea: DNA can be extracted from fruit by crushing it, mixing it with detergent and salt, heating and filtering the mixture, and adding ice-cold ethanol. The DNA is not soluble in ethanol, so it **precipitates** as white strands.

blocks.text: This practical releases DNA from fruit cells and makes it visible. This section covers the steps in order.

items.text: Grind or squash the fruit (a pestle and mortar can be used) to break up the cells.
Mix the crushed fruit with washing up liquid and salt solution. A protease enzyme can also be added.
Place it in a water bath, at about 60 °C.
Filter the mixture and keep the liquid (the filtrate).
Pour the ethanol slowly down the side of the test tube, onto the filtrate.
The DNA appears where the liquids meet, as white strands.

items: Crush, add detergent and salt, heat, filter, then add ice-cold ethanol.
The DNA is seen as a white precipitate.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask for the reason behind a step. Learn the job of each one.

rows: Breaks down the fruit and the cells (homogenises them), so the detergent can reach the cell membranes.
Breaks open the cell membranes, releasing the DNA.
Helps the DNA strands clump together, so that they can be seen.
Breaks down proteins in the cell and nuclear membranes. It also destroys enzymes that may break down the DNA.
Denatures enzymes that could break down the DNA. It is done in a water bath, at about 60 °C.
Removes the solid pieces of fruit. This gives the liquid (the filtrate) that contains the DNA.
DNA is insoluble in ethanol, so it **precipitates** and becomes visible.

items: Detergent breaks open the cell membranes, and salt helps the DNA clump together.
Protease breaks down proteins and destroys enzymes that could damage the DNA.
Ethanol is used to precipitate the DNA.

checks.q: State why ice-cold ethanol is added to the filtrate.
checks.a: To precipitate the DNA. DNA is insoluble in ethanol, so it can be seen.

checks.q: Explain why the enzyme protease is added to the mixture.
checks.a: It breaks down proteins in the cell or nuclear membrane, and it destroys enzymes that may break down the DNA.

checks.q: A student compares the mass of DNA from strawberries and kiwi fruit. Give two variables the student must control.

worked_example.question:
DNA is found in the nucleus of cells.

Describe the structure of DNA and how it can be extracted from plant cells.
answer_points: Structure: DNA is a polymer made of two strands in a double helix.
It is made of nucleotides, with four bases (A, T, C and G).
The bases form complementary base pairs, A with T and C with G, joined by weak hydrogen bonds.
Extraction: crush up (grind or squash) the cells.
Add detergent, salt solution or protease, and heat in a water bath (about 60 °C).
Add the mixture to ice-cold ethanol. The DNA forms a white precipitate (white strands).
